newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania minister attacked as protests grow.
newsitem.headline: Albania minister attacked as protests grow.

text.p: Demonstrators attacked Albanian Foreign Minister Tritan Shehu in the southern town of Lushnje on Saturday as protests over collapsing pyramid investment schemes spread across the Balkan state.
Shehu, chairman of the ruling Democratic Party, was hit by a hard object and his face was covered in blood, a witness said.
He went to the town, 85 km (55 miles) south of Tirana, to try and calm protesters infuriated at losing savings in dubious investment schemes promising high rates of interest.
"Shehu was attacked...when they recognised him. He must have been hit by a stone or hard object because his face is covered with blood," the witness said.
The foreign minister, together with bodyguards and plainclothes policemen, locked himself in the locker room of Lushnje town soccer stadium to prevent the crowd reaching him.
In Berat, 40 km (25 miles) south of Lushnje, crowds set fire to buildings in the town centre, Albanian television said.
A resident told Reuters by telephone that the town hall, prefecture and police station were ablaze.
"I am sorry for the policemen. They are beating them up. They have also taken the police chief hostage," a woman who lived near the police station said.
She said thousands had gathered earlier at the police station and a police helicopter was overhead but unable to land. Prisoners in the cells were freed or fled when the fire spread.
The crowd chanted anti-government slogans, "Down with the thieves!", "They have to give us our money back!".
Albania has been hit by two weeks of protests over the collapsing pyramid schemes, into which thousands of unsuspecting Albanians poured their life savings.
The protests intensified in Lushnje on Friday night when local residents set the town hall ablaze.
Shehu's visit was an attempt to calm the situation in the town but it seemed that the minister had little chance of addressing the crowd, which turned on him as soon as he was recognised.
